note: Engineering-reviewed admissible material and process search space. Baseline material/process values are synchronised with the frozen B4 pilot benchmark. Dimension envelopes marked CONFIRM are not active optimisation variables.

parts.engineering_context: Safety-relevant bracket under concentrated driver leg-load during braking. Bolted, non-axisymmetric geometry.

admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: current baseline — good machinability/weldability, adequate strength for a milled bracket
admissible_materials.AL_7075_T6: standard motorsport substitution for higher load margin; less weldable but this part is milled/bolted, not welded, so that limitation does not apply

inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: flat composite plate stock is not a validated substitute for a bolted, concentrated-load bracket without a proper laminate/layup design this project has not performed
inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: polymer stiffness/strength inadequate for a safety-relevant, concentrated-load structural bracket

admissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: current baseline — correct for this 3D bracket geometry

inadmissible_processes.CNC_TURNING: NOT ALLOWED — turning produces axisymmetric parts; this bracket's geometry is not axisymmetric (matches Person A's own worked example)

parts.engineering_context: Safety-relevant, fatigue-loaded suspension hard point. Cyclic loading over a race weekend makes fatigue life, not just static strength, the governing concern.

admissible_materials.STEEL_4130_CRMO: preferred for a fatigue-critical suspension pickup — better fatigue tolerance and weldability than aluminium alloys at this stress level
admissible_materials.AL_7075_T6: admissible only if the part is bolted rather than welded, given 7075's comparatively poor fatigue/weld behaviour; flag for review if the current design is welded

inadmissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: lower strength margin than 4130 or 7075 for a fatigue-critical suspension hard point — flag for review, do not assume inadmissible without confirming actual load case
inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: composite proxy has no established fatigue data in this project; do not use for a fatigue-critical safety part without further evidence
inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: polymer inadequate for a suspension load path

admissible_processes.TIG_WELDING: admissible only for the STEEL_4130_CRMO option, and only if the design is welded rather than bolted — confirm actual design

dimension_envelope.thickness_mm: CONFIRM — not established in prior project data

parts.engineering_context: Bolted or welded tab attaching a component to the chassis structure; moderate, largely static load.

admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: standard choice for a moderately loaded, weldable/machinable mounting tab
admissible_materials.STEEL_4130_CRMO: admissible where the tab is welded directly to a steel chassis tube, for weld-material compatibility — confirm chassis material before selecting

inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: no established basis for a welded/bolted tab application
inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: inadequate for a structural chassis attachment

admissible_processes.WATERJET_CUT: suitable if the tab is a simple flat profile rather than requiring 3D milled features — confirm actual geometry
admissible_processes.TIG_WELDING: admissible only for the STEEL_4130_CRMO option if welded to a steel chassis

parts.engineering_context: Structural gusset bracing the roll-hoop, a primary occupant-safety structure under FSG rules. This is one of the least appropriate parts in the whole benchmark for aggressive material substitution given its direct safety role.

admissible_materials.STEEL_4130_CRMO: standard roll-hoop-adjacent material choice for strength and weldability to a steel roll-hoop
admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: admissible only if the roll-hoop itself is aluminium and the gusset is welded/bolted to match — confirm roll-hoop material before allowing this substitution

inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: composite substitution for a roll-hoop bracing element requires a level of structural validation (layup, energy absorption) this project has not performed — flag as inadmissible pending dedicated analysis, not a routine optimiser choice
inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: wholly inadequate for a primary occupant-safety structural element

admissible_processes.TIG_WELDING: standard for a roll-hoop-adjacent steel gusset
admissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: admissible if the gusset is a machined rather than welded component — confirm actual design

dimension_envelope.note: safety-critical part — recommend a narrower envelope than the standard ±30% used elsewhere, pending explicit supervisor/reviewer sign-off given the roll-hoop safety role

parts.engineering_context: Small spacer on the steering column; low structural load, primarily a positioning/clearance part.

admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: standard low-load spacer material, easy to machine
admissible_materials.NYLON_PA6: admissible for a genuinely low-load spacer if the design does not rely on the spacer for structural stiffness — confirm the part's actual load path before allowing a polymer substitution on any steering-adjacent component

inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: no engineering benefit for a simple low-load spacer; unnecessary cost/complexity

admissible_processes.CNC_TURNING: appropriate if the spacer is axisymmetric (a typical spacer/bushing form)
admissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: appropriate if the spacer has a non-axisymmetric or keyed profile

dimension_envelope.note: CONFIRM — not established in prior project data

parts.engineering_context: Bushing carrying wheel-bearing loads — safety-relevant, moderate-to-high cyclic load, close dimensional tolerance for bearing fit.

admissible_materials.STEEL_4130_CRMO: preferred for a bearing-carrier application given wear resistance and fatigue behaviour under cyclic wheel loads
admissible_materials.AL_7075_T6: admissible only where a bearing insert/sleeve is used rather than the bushing bore itself acting as the wear surface — confirm design before allowing, since aluminium alone is a poor direct bearing-bore material

inadmissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: insufficient wear resistance for a direct bearing bore surface — flag for review rather than assume, pending confirmation of actual bearing interface design
inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: flat-plate composite proxy has no established relevance to a turned bushing/bearing-carrier geometry
inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: inadequate load capacity for a wheel-bearing carrier

admissible_processes.CNC_TURNING: correct process for an axisymmetric bushing with a precision bore

inadmissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: not the natural process for a precision axisymmetric bushing bore; admissible only for non-round features on the same part, not the bore itself

dimension_envelope.note: bore tolerance is bearing-fit-critical — recommend a narrow, bearing-catalogue-driven envelope rather than the standard ±30%, pending confirmation of the actual bearing part number (cf. the MISUMI-sourced bearing precedent already in this project)

parts.engineering_context: Standoff mounting an aerodynamic component; low-to-moderate load, mass-sensitive since it is unsprung/high aero-relevant mass.

admissible_materials.AL_7075_T6: admissible where higher strength-to-weight is wanted, e.g. a longer or more loaded standoff
admissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: admissible as a mass-reduction option given this part's low structural criticality relative to the roll-hoop/suspension parts above, but the composite proxy's realistic small-batch cost (Section 7.7.1 elsewhere in this project) should be factored into any cost-driven optimiser comparison

inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: insufficient stiffness for an aero-load-bearing standoff, which must resist aerodynamic deflection, not just static weight

admissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: suitable for a standoff with mounting features at both ends
admissible_processes.CNC_TURNING: suitable if the standoff is a simple axisymmetric post

parts.engineering_context: Composite panel already established in this project as using the CF_PLATE_3K retail proxy material (Section 7.7.1, Section 5.5.6 elsewhere in this project). Enclosure panel, not a primary load path, but must contain the battery in a crash event.

admissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: current baseline, already established and cost-analysed elsewhere in this project
admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: admissible heavier alternative if composite small-batch cost/availability is a concern for this part specifically

inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: insufficient impact/containment performance for a battery enclosure panel without further evidence

dimension_envelope.note: CONFIRM — panel geometry, likely area/thickness rather than a simple envelope

parts.engineering_context: Already established elsewhere in this project as a PA6 filament FDM part (Section 10.14.1's conflation-trap example distinguishes NYLON_PA6_FILAMENT from NYLON_PA6 precisely because this part uses the filament form). Low load, sensor-carrying bracket.

admissible_materials.NYLON_PA6_FILAMENT: admissible nylon filament option for FDM printing

inadmissible_materials.PA6_SHEET: wrong form for this process — sheet stock is not FDM filament; this is precisely the conflation this project's B9 fine-tuning trap example was built to catch, and should never be silently substituted here
inadmissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: admissible only if the process is also changed away from FDM — metal FDM/machining is a different process entry, not a material swap alone

admissible_processes.FDM_3DPRINT: current baseline, correct for a low-load sensor bracket

inadmissible_processes.CNC_MILLING: admissible only paired with a material change to a millable stock, not as a same-material process swap

parts.engineering_context: Already established elsewhere in this project as fastener-cost-dominated — the single fastener costs more than the part's combined material and process cost (Section 7.5.9 elsewhere in this project). Very low load, positioning/retention only.

admissible_materials.AL_6061_T6: admissible but likely an unnecessary cost/mass increase for a pure retention clip — flag as low-value substitution

inadmissible_materials.CF_PLATE_3K: no engineering benefit for a low-load retention clip; composite proxy cost would dominate for no functional gain
inadmissible_materials.STEEL_4130_CRMO: unnecessary mass/cost for a low-load clip

admissible_processes.FDM_3DPRINT: suitable low-cost option for a simple low-load clip geometry

dimension_envelope.note: CONFIRM — given this part's cost is fastener-dominated rather than material/process-dominated, dimensional optimisation here has limited leverage regardless of envelope chosen
